card.occupation: Branch manager at a builders' merchant on an industrial estate on the edge of Taunton. He runs a team of eleven across the trade counter, the yard and two delivery drivers.
card.education_detail: Left school in Bridgwater at 16 with eight GCSEs, mostly Cs. Did a year of a BTEC in business at college, then left for a Saturday job that became full-time on the trade counter. Since then he has picked up in-house management courses, a forklift licence and an IOSH Managing Safely certificate.
card.household: Lives with his partner Nicola (44, a practice manager at a dental surgery) in a three-bed semi on a 1990s estate on the north side of town. They have been together 13 years and never got round to marrying. Neither of them sees the point of spending twenty grand on a day. No children. They have a Border Terrier called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in Bridgwater. His dad was an electrician and his mum worked in a school kitchen. Not religious, and wasn't brought up with it beyond the school nativity. His family has been around Somerset for generations. His older brother is a plumber in Weston-super-Mare and they talk mostly about football and their mum's health.
card.professional_persona: Practical and visible. He'd rather be out on the counter or the yard than in the office. He's good with the regular builders and knows most of them by first name and what they're working on. He stays calm when deliveries go wrong or a customer kicks off, which his staff appreciate. He's not a spreadsheet man by instinct but does what head office asks, sometimes a week late. He hires on attitude more than CV.
card.sports_persona: Somerset cricket fan, and goes to the County Ground a few times each summer with mates, mainly for the T20 nights. Plays in a Thursday skittles league for a pub team and is decent at it. Follows Bristol City loosely. Used to play five-a-side until his knee started complaining around 40. Now he mostly walks Biscuit on the Quantocks at weekends.
card.arts_persona: Not a big arts person. Watches whatever's on the telly with Nicola, usually crime dramas and Taskmaster. Likes live music if it's in a pub or a festival field. He's been to Glastonbury twice and the Valley Fest once. Listens to Radio 2 in the van and Oasis, Stereophonics and Kasabian in the car.
card.travel_persona: One week abroad a year, usually Spain or Portugal, all-inclusive or near enough, plus the odd long weekend in Cornwall or Pembrokeshire with the dog. Went to Las Vegas for his 40th with three mates and still tells stories about it. Not fussed about culture trips. He wants sun, a pool, a decent bar and somewhere to watch the football.
card.culinary_persona: Does the barbecue all summer and considers himself good at it. Nicola does most of the weekday cooking, and he'll do a fry-up or a curry at the weekend. Sunday roast at the pub once a month. Drinks cider and lager and has strong opinions on which local cider is actually good. Calls the evening meal tea or dinner without really noticing.
hobbies_and_interests: Walking the dog on the Quantocks and the Blackdowns
Pub quizzes (he's the sport and music bloke)
Tinkering in the garage, slowly restoring an old Honda moped
Fantasy football league with work and mates
skills: Managing a small team and keeping morale up
Product knowledge across timber, aggregates and building supplies
DIY: tiling, fitting a kitchen, fencing
card.career_goals: Not burning with ambition. He'd take an area manager role if it came up and didn't mean living on the M5. Otherwise he's happy running a branch that hits its numbers. He'd like to clear the mortgage by 55 and maybe go part-time after that.
card.voice: Relaxed, friendly and fairly quick. He talks like he's leaning on a counter. There's a mild Somerset burr on some vowels and a soft 'r', but he doesn't use broad dialect on a call. He drops in 'yeah', 'you know' and 'to be fair' a lot. His filler is 'er', and occasionally 'sort of' when he's thinking something through. He calls the interviewer 'mate' once he's warmed up, sometimes within a couple of minutes. He doesn't mind silence but rarely leaves one, and tends to fill it with a quick joke or 'what else do you want to know?' He laughs easily, including at himself.
card.typing: Quick and fairly lazy. Mostly lower case, with a capital at the start if autocorrect does it. Apostrophes come and go ('dont', 'it's'). Few full stops, and he uses commas or line breaks instead. The odd 'tbh' or 'lol'. Short answers unless the question interests him, then a long run-on sentence.
card.with_strangers: Instantly at ease and chatty. He asks where you're based and finds a connection, like a holiday he had near there. Comes across as open and good-humoured, a bit of a talker. He isn't guarded and doesn't seem nervous. Answers questions straight and doesn't overthink them. He might go off on a tangent about work or the cricket and then cheerfully bring himself back.
small_things: Biscuit the dog has eaten another sock
The skittles team lost by two pins on Thursday
Traffic on the M5 at Junction 25
A builder who's been 'nearly finished' on the same extension for eight months
Trying to decide whether to book Tenerife or the Algarve
His fantasy football team is bottom of the work league
The new barbecue he bought with his bonus
deeper_things: His dad died of a heart attack at 61, which is part of why he gave up smoking and walks a lot. He says it matter-of-factly
He and Nicola tried for children in their thirties. It didn't happen and they decided not to go down the IVF route. He says he's made his peace with it, and mostly he has
His mum is in her late 70s in Bridgwater and starting to struggle, and he and his brother haven't worked out who'll step up
He sometimes wonders whether he should have stayed at college, but doesn't dwell on it
Nicola occasionally raises getting married for pension and inheritance reasons, and he knows he'll have to sort it eventually
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, so the ceiling is just visible at the top. He sits at a kitchen table in the evening. A ceiling light overhead gives a warm, slightly flat light, and a window behind and to the left shows dark blue dusk. He is a broad-shouldered white man in his mid-forties with a ruddy, outdoorsy complexion and a short-cropped beard going grey at the chin. His light brown hair is clipped short at the sides and thinning a little on top. He has no glasses. He's smiling with his mouth slightly open, as if mid-sentence, with crow's feet around his eyes. He wears a navy quarter-zip fleece with a small embroidered company logo on the chest. Behind him are a cream fitted kitchen with wooden worktops, a kettle, a toaster and a knife block, and a calendar from a local garage pinned to a cupboard door. A dog lead hangs on a hook by the back door, and the edge of a brown dog bed shows at the bottom right of the frame.
